# Torben Fennmere

Torben Fennmere is a Contract Automation Engineer at Tesstun Works, a leading AI-powered platform specializing in automating clause extraction and redlining for procurement teams. Since joining Tesstun Works in 2021, Torben has played a pivotal role in advancing the company’s core AI models that enable precise identification and extraction of contractual clauses across diverse legal documents.

Career History  
Torben began his career in 2014 as a software developer focusing on machine learning applications in document analysis. From 2017 to 2021, he was a senior engineer at ClearLex Solutions, where he led the deployment of their neural redlining system, codenamed “Project Crimson Slate.” This system revolutionized how procurement and legal teams reviewed contracts by enabling real-time, AI-driven redline suggestions. Under his direction, Crimson Slate improved contract review speeds by over 35% in pilot deployments.

Specialties  
Torben’s expertise centers around developing and fine-tuning deep learning models specifically designed for clause extraction and contract comparison tasks. He is skilled in natural language processing techniques tailored to legal text, including transformer-based architectures and domain adaptation strategies. His work emphasizes model explainability to ensure legal professionals can trust the AI’s recommendations.

Notable Projects  
- “Project Onyx Extractor”: A proprietary clause extraction model launched at Tesstun Works that improved recall rates by 18% over previous benchmarks.  
- “Rapid Redline”: A module integrated into the Tesstun platform that offers near-instantaneous contract redlining suggestions with high accuracy.  
- “ProcureVision Analytics”: An internal analytics suite co-developed by Torben to visualize clause trends and flag high-risk provisions during procurement reviews.

Working Style and Collaboration  
Known for a collaborative approach, Torben works closely with data scientists, legal experts, and product managers to align AI capabilities with user needs. He actively mentors junior engineers and regularly contributes to cross-functional workshops aimed at bridging legal domain knowledge with technical development. His problem-solving style is methodical, emphasizing iterative testing and user feedback integration to refine models continuously.
